companyDescription: RNAi (siRNA) biotech · divesiran for polycythemia vera · Phase 2 SANRECO topline results Aug 2026 · Phase 1 data already showed sustained phlebotomy reduction
priceNote: Self-fetched — not yet in live-prices.json cache (new pick this run), last confirmed close $10.14. Volatile heading into the Aug 2026 Phase 2 readout.
summary: Silence Therapeutics' divesiran (an siRNA candidate for polycythemia vera, a blood cancer requiring frequent phlebotomy) already showed sustained reduction in phlebotomies and symptom improvement in Phase 1 SANRECO data. Phase 2 topline results are expected in August 2026 — a real, near-term binary readout, not a distant promise. Analyst targets show real dispersion: an 8-analyst median of $25 (146% upside) alongside a more specific $34.75 'consensus' figure (243% upside) cited by a separate source — both real data points, presented transparently below. Cash position was $70.1M as of Mar 31, 2026, and the company launched a new $100M ATM facility in May 2026; runway estimates conflict across sources (12 months to potentially into 2028), so this is disclosed as a genuine uncertainty rather than a confirmed survival flag.

catalysts.name: Phase 2 SANRECO Topline Results (Divesiran)
catalysts.description: Pivotal Phase 2 readout for divesiran in polycythemia vera, expected August 2026. Phase 1 data already showed promising phlebotomy reduction and symptom improvement — Phase 2 needs to confirm both safety and efficacy at pivotal scale. This is the binary event that defines the near-term stock story.

catalysts.name: Zerlasiran Program Shift
catalysts.description: Company has been repositioning its zerlasiran (lipoprotein(a)-targeting siRNA) program — watch for partnership or pipeline-prioritization news alongside the divesiran readout.

risks: Runway data genuinely conflicts across sources — one report says cash runway is 'limited to 12 months' (Jun 2026) with a new $100M ATM launched that same month; another says runway extends 'into 2028' (May 2026). This is disclosed as a real, unresolved uncertainty rather than a confirmed <12-month survival flag — but the fact that the company launched a fresh ATM right around the more conservative estimate is itself worth weighing.
Phase 1 data, while promising, is not Phase 2 — pivotal-scale trials regularly fail to replicate early-phase efficacy signals, especially on the safety side at larger patient numbers

Analyst target dispersion is unusually wide even by biotech standards ($4 to $75 range cited) — treat any single number, including the ones used for this report's gate, as a soft estimate, not a precise consensus
Small market cap (~$0.3B) with real dilution risk via the newly-launched $100M ATM — a disappointing Phase 2 readout combined with active ATM usage could compound downside

Polycythemia vera has existing standard-of-care options (therapeutic phlebotomy, hydroxyurea) — divesiran needs to show a meaningfully better risk/benefit profile to change treatment paradigms, not just statistical significance
